independentReview.reviewerNote: THIRD review of this branch, and the first to find nothing. It verified by MUTATION, not by reading. (1) No serde attribute can hide a field from the new whole-row catch-all: it read AppliedChangeView (bare derive(Serialize), no field-level attributes) plus HwFingerprint / Snapshot / AppliedAction / RollbackAction, then proved the claim by drifting a NESTED sub-field this lane never mutated -- hw_fingerprint.gpu_driver, chosen because same_rig deliberately ignores it so on_this_rig stays identical on both sides -- RED, caught by the catch-all with the gpu_driver value visible in the assertion diff. (2) The catch-all does not relocate a computed-field failure: forcing restores_label to Some("MUTATED-LABEL") still failed at its own named assert, not at the catch-all. (3) `expected` (loop) and `reference` (canary) are both derived from `rows` via into_view directly, never from the projection's own output, so neither can answer a question about itself. (4) Fixture: every row still earns its place; visual-effects/rolled_back is the only row proving the not-applied short-circuit of check_change_active. Two non-blocking observations, neither owed a fix: three rows incidentally share the unknown-rec-id arm of is_still_active while keeping distinct primary purposes, and a pre-existing pattern -- not introduced here -- where game-mode and now fast-startup-off read live OS state inside a unit test.
independentReview.orchestratorCorroboration: This lane did not take the APPROVE on trust, and did not take the two CHANGES REQUIRED verdicts on trust either. Round 2 (restores_label / applied_label / payoff_label vacuous) was confirmed against the code before acting -- record() sets applied_action None and a snapshot that cannot deserialize to any Snapshot variant, so both label derivations short-circuit at `action.as_ref()?` -- and reproduced by mutation. Round 3 (ten carried-across fields unguarded) was likewise reproduced. Round 2's OTHER finding was NOT accepted: it asked for a fixture row to catch a narrowed same_rig; this lane built that row, measured that it does not discriminate, deleted it rather than keep a row that looks like coverage without being coverage, and recorded the structural reason instead -- both sides of the loop reach same_rig through the same into_view call, so no fixture row can catch it. The third reviewer independently confirmed that, and further showed a total collapse of same_rig to constant true IS caught by the canary. Falsification counts for all 14 fields are posted on the PR at comments 5580599540 and 5580799217.

falsificationNote: The bug-to-guard law was satisfied by measurement in both directions at every head, never by a green run alone. Pre-patch, the original blind spot was reproduced independently: forcing on_this_rig = None inside applied_change_views left the guard GREEN at 2 passed / 0 failed. At this head all 14 fields of the projection go RED when mutated one at a time inside applied_change_views -- the four computed-at-read fields each at their own named assert (history.rs:2343 restores_label, :2344 applied_label, :2345 payoff_label, :2346 on_this_rig), and the ten carried-across fields (rec_title, applied_at, snapshot, applied_action, rollback_action, app_version_at_apply, ruleset_version_at_apply, elevation_used, hw_fingerprint, rolled_back_at) at the whole-row catch-all -- each 0 passed / 1 failed, the file restored between every mutation and the tree verified clean after. Two methodological corrections are recorded rather than buried. A first falsification script used `git checkout --` to clean up while its subject patch was still uncommitted, so three of its four results measured an unpatched file; it was caught from a line-number mismatch, the patch was committed first, and the run repeated with a dirty-tree abort guard. A first rec_title mutation also failed to COMPILE (Some(x) written for a String field), which prints no test result at all and would have read as not-caught in the table; re-run with the correct type, it went RED.
mutationBoundaryNote: history.rs is a starred mutation/rollback-boundary module, so the boundary was checked explicitly even though this change is test-only. `git diff main...HEAD --stat` is one file, 99 insertions and 0 deletions, every hunk between `#[cfg(test)]` (line 2183) and the end of mod history_tests. No production line changed, no apply_ / rollback_ / dispatch_rollback / resolve_rollback / run_elevated / save_history call site added or altered, no new #[tauri::command], no capability change, and no derive added to a production struct -- the catch-all compares the serialized form precisely because adding PartialEq to AppliedChangeView would have been a production change this lane is not scoped for.
